data.scenario_text: A zipline runs in a straight line from the top of a launch platform to an anchor point on the ground. The zipline is <m>160</m> feet long, and the angle of depression from the top of the platform to the anchor point is <m>21^\circ</m>.
data.part_b: Explain how to place the given <m>21^\circ</m> angle inside the right triangle, then state which trigonometric ratio connects the known sides to the height of the platform.
data.part_c: Find the height of the platform. Do not round until the final answer; then round to two decimal places.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). A correct sketch shows a right triangle with the 21^\circ angle at the correct vertex, the side opposite it of length 57.34 ft, the side adjacent to it of length 149.37 ft, and the hypotenuse @sh@ ft.

Part (b). The angle of depression is measured downward from a horizontal line through the top of the platform. That line is parallel to the ground, so the angle of depression and the angle of elevation from the anchor point are alternate interior angles and are therefore congruent. The 21^\circ angle sits inside the triangle at the anchor point. The known side is the hypotenuse and the unknown is the height of the platform, so the ratio that connects them is sine: \sin\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}.

Part (c). h=160\sin(21^\circ) \approx 57.34\text{ ft}

So the height of the platform is \boxed{57.34\text{ ft}}.

data.part_c: Find the horizontal distance from the boat to the foot of the lighthouse. Do not round until the final answer; then round to two decimal places.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). A correct sketch shows a right triangle with the 22^\circ angle at the correct vertex, the side opposite it of length 160 ft, the side adjacent to it of length 396.01 ft, and the hypotenuse @sh@ ft.

Part (b). The angle of depression is measured downward from a horizontal line through the top of the lighthouse. Because that line is parallel to the surface of the sea, alternate interior angles give a congruent angle of elevation at the boat, so the 22^\circ angle is the one inside the triangle at the boat. The known side is the leg opposite the given angle and the unknown is the horizontal distance from the boat to the foot of the lighthouse, so the ratio that connects them is tangent: \tan\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}.

Part (c). d=\frac{160}{\tan(22^\circ)} \approx 396.01\text{ ft}

So the horizontal distance from the boat to the foot of the lighthouse is \boxed{396.01\text{ ft}}.
